lead.label: 1c, ALM-844
lead.why: Abstract: 'The most active compounds among the new series were ALM-844 [N1,N5-bis(2,3,4-trimethoxybenzyl)pentane-1,5-diamine dihydrochloride] and ALM-851 [...]'; ALM-844 is the first one named. ALM-851 (1a) is also named, so the lead is a two-way tie broken by order of mention.

reactions.conditions: Aldehyde (2 equiv, 77 mmol) and diamine (1 equiv, 35 mmol) in EtOH, 1 h rt, then H2 (1 atm), PdO/C (10% Pd), rt until H2 uptake stops; filtrate evaporated, solid dissolved in Me2CO, conc. HCl added to acidic, precipitate filtered and recrystallised from i-PrOH. Yield 59%. Reported as one general procedure (reductive amination and salt formation), counted as one step.
reactions.source: Experimental chemical part, p. 332 (general method and 1c entry); Scheme 1

alt_variants.conditions: Same procedure without the final HCl salt formation (the base is not isolated in the paper; salt formation is part of the same procedure).

notes: The 1c heading in the text prints 'pentane-1,3-diamine' but the abstract and the text 'prepared from ... 1,5-pentanediamine' and formula C25H40Cl2N2O6 all say 1,5; I used the abstract's name. The abstract also calls ALM-851 'propane-1,4-diamine' while the experimental says propane-1,3-diamine (the same slip). Stoichiometry: 2 aldehydes per diamine, both aldehyde-derived benzyl groups in the product. Amines are not described as commercial explicitly (no supplier statement) but are used with no preparation. | EDITED 2026-10-24: aldehyde listed twice (2 equiv incorporated); the hydrochloride salt formation is not part of the compared structure (free base).
